cim: Los Angeles schools block Google’s AI features. BSF received more than 20,000 emails on the subject.
cim_eredeti: Los Angeles schools block Google’s AI features. BSF received more than 20,000 emails on the subject.
szoveg_eredeti:
WORLD ORGANIZATION BULLYING SIN FRONTERAS

The decision renews concerns over artificial intelligence in education, student learning and the influence of major technology companies on school systems.

Education officials in Los Angeles have disabled Google's AI-generated search summaries on school-issued devices, deepening the debate between school districts and the technology giant over the use of artificial intelligence in education.

Sources connected to the Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD), one of the largest school systems in the United States, with approximately half a million students, confirmed to Bullying Sin Fronteras that the district had disabled Google's AI Overview feature, which provides AI-generated summaries and answers directly within search results.

BULLYING SIN FRONTERAS HAS RECEIVED MORE THAN 20,000 EMAILS FROM PARENTS AND TEACHERS IN LOS ANGELES ABOUT THIS ISSUE.

Thousands of parents, teachers and people connected to the education community have contacted Bullying Sin Fronteras seeking guidance on how to respond to the growing use of artificial intelligence in school tools.

In most of these messages, deep concern is expressed about student learning, the ability to develop critical thinking skills, and the intellectual authorship of assignments and assessments.

It is a simple question: If AI can solve everything, what are students learning at school?

The school district said the temporary suspension is intended to ensure that students have age-appropriate and safe digital experiences.

Google maintains that its search engine and artificial intelligence tools are deeply integrated and that it is not possible to completely separate the two services within the educational environment.

This position has raised concerns among school officials who want to preserve access to traditional search tools without automatically incorporating AI-generated answers.

Artificial intelligence can be an extraordinary tool. However, when it begins to systematically replace intellectual effort, research, reasoning, writing and the development of original ideas, schools face a challenge they cannot ignore.

The issue is not merely technological. It is educational.

Schools must teach students how to use tools, but also how to think without them, question answers, investigate, understand, make mistakes and build knowledge of their own.

The possibility of replacing Google search with alternative services remains open to school districts.

The debate unfolding in Los Angeles reflects a dilemma increasingly facing educational systems around the world: how to incorporate technology without delegating essential processes of learning, critical thinking and the intellectual development of children and adolescents.

Bullying Sin Fronteras offers an answer in the form of a question:

If AI can solve everything, what will students learn at school?

Information provided by the Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD).
